newsitem.title: USA: Low jobless rate worries Wall St too much - Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Low jobless rate worries Wall St too much - Jordan.

text.p: Wall Street analysts may be the only group still concerned with the notion that low unemployment fuels inflation, Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Jerry Jordan said on Thursday.
"I hear a lot of commentary on Wall Street about those kind of things," Jordan told Reuters, answering a question about the possible relationship between a low unemployment rate and rising inflation.
"Maybe the Wall Street analysts, the people that talk to (financial cable news network) CNBC, are just talking to each other. Maybe no one else is listening," Jordan added.

According to a school of economists, a U.S. unemployment rate steadily below 5.75 percent fuels inflationary pressures. The jobless has been no higher than 5.8 percent since September 1994 without evidence of rising inflation.
Jordan further cautioned against Wall Street's perception of what guides U.S. monetary policy at the moment.
"There are people (on) the Street that have past Fed experience and a good understanding and people that are guessing," the Cleveland Fed president added.

Jordan said the Fed is "trying to create the conditions where people make their decisions about the future in the expectation that the purchasing power of the currency will be about the same as it is now."
